newsitem.title: UK: Mobutu's fortune peaked at $4 billion - FT.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu's fortune peaked at $4 billion - FT.

text.p: Decades of embezzling by Zaire's ruling elite allowed President Mobutu Sese Seko to accumulate a personal fortune which peaked at $4 billion in the mid-1980s, the Financial Times newspaper said on Monday.

The FT, reporting on the results of its own investigation into Mobutu's wealth, said the estimates of his fortune were made by officials from the United States Treasury and International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The newspaper said the ailing Mobutu, suffering from prostate cancer, had spent much of the fortune trying to prop up his regime, which came under pressure from the mid-1980s from falling revenues and pressure to implement democratic reforms.
"Much of the fortune has been spent as the ailing dictator has attempted to prop up his regime, now thought to be on the verge of collapse as rebels advanced on the capital Kinshasa," the FT said.
The newspaper said it had identified at least 20 properties owned by Mobutu and his close entourage which were worth a minimum of 23 million pounds ($36 million).
It said western governments and financial institutions had provided support and aid to Mubutu despite clear evidence that the country's national wealth was being systematically stolen.

Although a senior IMF official said in 1982 that Zaire was endemically corrupt, western governments continued to support loans totalling $3.9 billion in multilateral and bilateral aid between 1982 and 1991, the paper said.
